title: Taylor Swift’s Song of the Year Grammy Quip Was Likely No Accident
summary: Was Swift just striking a note of humility or was she signaling that she really, really wants to win in that category?
contentText:
Taylor Swift had the honor of announcing the final two categories on Monday’s (Nov. 16) livestream of nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards. “The last two categories to be announced — one of them I’ve had a lot of luck in, the other one I’m zero-for-eight,” she said. “Here are the nominees for album [of the year] and song of the year.”

It was a winning remark – amusing and lightly self-deprecating. Perhaps Swift was just striking a note of humility, reminding the audience that, for all her enormous success, she doesn’t win ’em all. Or was it more than that? Was Swift signaling that she really, really wants to win song of the year after eight losses in the category? She has had more nominations without a win than anyone else in the history of the category, a distinction she’d probably like to shed.

It echoes the situation on the Grammy telecast in February 2024 where Jay-Z pointedly reminded the audience that Beyoncé had never won album of the year, despite four previous nominations in that category. Beyoncé finally won album of the year the very next year with Cowboy Carter . She was overdue for a win in the category, it’s true, but Jay may have helped clinch the award for her by signaling just how much it meant to her. Even though Bey had won 32 Grammys at that point (she has since won three more), she really wanted to win what many consider to be the most prestigious Grammy.

Swift has won album of the year a record four times, but she has never won song of the year, even though many consider her to be the songwriter of her generation. In June, she became the second-youngest person ever to be inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, behind only Stevie Wonder . (Quick aside: Wonder hasn’t won a Grammy for song of the year, either.)

If Swift were to win song of the year for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which she co-wrote with frequent collaborator Jack Antonoff , it might help her clinch the Oscar for best original song, another award she has made no secret of wanting. The Grammys will be presented on Feb. 7. Final-round voting for the Oscars opens 18 days later, on Feb. 25. Swift can win the Oscar without first winning a Grammy, but who wouldn’t want to win both? (The last song to win both was Billie Eilish and Finneas ’ Barbie ballad “What Was I Made For?”)

As a bonus, here are Swift’s eight nominations for song of the year, along with the song that won that year. You can judge for yourself if she was robbed or merely lost to another worthy nominee. (The year shown is the year of the Grammy ceremony. We show only the artist’s name for simplicity’s sake, but the award goes to all the songwriters.)

- 2010: “You Belong With Me” (lost to Beyoncé’s “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)”)

- 2015: “Shake It Off” (lost to Sam Smith’s “Stay With Me”)

- 2016: “Blank Space” (lost to Ed Sheeran’s “Thinking Out Loud”)

- 2020: “Lover” (lost to Billie Eilish’s “Bad Guy”)

- 2021: “Cardigan” (lost to H.E.R.’s “I Can’t Breathe”)

- 2023: “All Too Well (10 Minute Version)” (lost to Bonnie Raitt’s “Just Like That”)

- 2024: “Anti-Hero” (lost to Billie Eilish’s “What Was I Made For”?)

- 2025: “Fortnight” (lost to Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us”)

Here’s a second bonus: The people who have amassed the most nominations in four other “General Field” categories without yet winning in that category.

- Record of the year: Beyoncé (nine nods)

- Album of the year: Lady Gaga, Kendrick Lamar (five nods each)

- Producer of the year, non-classical: Nigel Godrich (five nods)

- Songwriter of the year, non-classical: Édgar Barrera (four nods, including one this year)
